desc: Derive and verify the characterization f(L,R) = (#distinct values) - (# of v such that both v and v+1 appear), including proof that one operation can erase any maximal run of consecutive present values and that fewer operations are impossible.
Implement the full solution: term1 = sum over subarrays of distinct count via last-occurrence sweep (add i - last[A_i] at each i, 1-indexed).

Build position lists pos[v]; for each v in 1..N-1 with both pos[v] and pos[v+1] nonempty, compute subarrays containing both via complement: total - avoid(P) - avoid(Q) + avoid(P∪Q), where avoid(S) = Σ g(g+1)/2 over gaps of positions not in S.
Combine answer = term1 - Σ_v both(v,v+1); verify on samples (16, 23, 129) and brute-force small random tests against direct f computation.
Finalize stdin/stdout code, check edge cases (N=1, all equal values, permutation, value N present).
